onboarding.methods.gtd.name: GTD
onboarding.methods.gtd.description: A method for turning everything that has your attention into clear, reviewable commitments and next actions.
onboarding.methods.gtd.example: A note about a broken chair becomes a project to get it repaired, a next action to contact a repair service, and a waiting item once you have requested a quote.
onboarding.methods.gtd.effort: Process captured items and review your lists regularly. Capturing more without clarifying and reviewing creates another backlog.
onboarding.methods.gtd.limits: GTD does not make every commitment fit into your available time, or replace a system for developing knowledge.
onboarding.methods.gtd.feature0: Capture: collect what has your attention in trusted places.
onboarding.methods.gtd.feature1: Clarify: decide what each item means and whether it needs action.
onboarding.methods.gtd.feature2: Organize: keep next actions, projects, waiting items and reference material where you can find them.
onboarding.methods.gtd.feature3: Reflect: review your commitments and keep the system current.
onboarding.methods.gtd.feature4: Engage: use that overview to choose what to do.
onboarding.methods.kanban.name: Personal Kanban
onboarding.methods.kanban.description: A visual way to understand your work and limit how much you take on at once.
onboarding.methods.kanban.example: A reading-corner project waits until one of your active projects is finished. Its card then moves into your active work.
onboarding.methods.kanban.effort: Keep the board current and respect your chosen active-work limit. The columns alone are not the method.
onboarding.methods.kanban.limits: A board does not automatically provide reminders, plan your calendar or decide which work matters most.
onboarding.methods.kanban.feature0: Make work visible rather than keeping it in your head.
onboarding.methods.kanban.feature1: Show how work moves through stages that fit your life.
onboarding.methods.kanban.feature2: Limit work in progress so starting something requires making room.
onboarding.methods.kanban.feature3: Notice blocked work and adjust the flow.
onboarding.methods.journal.name: Bullet Journal
onboarding.methods.journal.description: A notebook-based system that combines quick recording with reflection and deliberate decisions about unfinished work.
onboarding.methods.journal.example: At a monthly review, an unfinished reading task is either still worth carrying forward or no longer worth your attention.
onboarding.methods.journal.effort: Record regularly and make time to reconsider open entries. Migration is a decision, not just copying tasks to tomorrow.
onboarding.methods.journal.limits: A digital adaptation should preserve reflection without creating duplicate task lists. Bullet Journal does not automatically schedule your work.
onboarding.methods.journal.feature0: Rapid logging: short entries distinguish tasks, events and notes.
onboarding.methods.journal.feature1: An index and collections make related entries findable.
onboarding.methods.journal.feature2: Future, monthly and daily logs connect different planning horizons.
onboarding.methods.journal.feature3: Reflection and migration help you keep, move or drop unfinished commitments.
onboarding.methods.time-blocking.name: Time Blocking
onboarding.methods.time-blocking.descrip: Plan when you intend to work by giving activities a place in your available time.
onboarding.methods.time-blocking.example: Reserve the morning for writing a proposal, then a shorter block for messages. Replan the afternoon if the writing takes longer.
onboarding.methods.time-blocking.effort: Make a plan, check your estimates and adjust it as the day changes. The aim is intention, not a perfect schedule.
onboarding.methods.time-blocking.limits: A time block is not a deadline. This technique does not capture all commitments or organize your information; calendar changes need separate agreement.
onboarding.methods.time-blocking.feature: Divide the day into blocks and assign activities to them.
Account for existing appointments and other commitments.
Estimate how much time work will need.
Revise the remaining plan when interruptions or overruns occur.
onboarding.methods.pomodoro.name: Pomodoro
onboarding.methods.pomodoro.description: A time-management method for planning focused work, handling interruptions and learning from the effort it takes.
onboarding.methods.pomodoro.example: Choose a writing task, estimate the focus intervals it needs, work with breaks, then compare the actual effort with your estimate.
onboarding.methods.pomodoro.effort: Use the intervals, manage interruptions and reflect on the results. The full method is more than running a timer.
onboarding.methods.pomodoro.limits: Focus intervals do not decide which commitments deserve attention or how to organize your notes. A timer or notifications are separate tool choices.
onboarding.methods.pomodoro.feature0: Keep an activity inventory and choose work for today.
onboarding.methods.pomodoro.feature2: Work on one activity during timed focus intervals, with regular breaks.
onboarding.methods.pomodoro.feature3: Handle interruptions deliberately rather than switching unnoticed.
onboarding.methods.pomodoro.feature4: Record effort and compare estimates with experience.
onboarding.methods.eisenhower.name: Eisenhower Matrix
onboarding.methods.eisenhower.descriptio: A way to consider importance and urgency separately when deciding where to put your attention.
onboarding.methods.eisenhower.example: An important plan without an immediate deadline can deserve time before a stream of urgent but less meaningful requests.
onboarding.methods.eisenhower.effort: Make the judgments yourself and revisit them when circumstances change. Not every request will fit neatly into one quadrant.
onboarding.methods.eisenhower.limits: The matrix does not estimate effort or resolve dependencies. Delegating may not be possible; a quadrant is not permission to delegate or delete anything.
onboarding.methods.eisenhower.feature0: Judge importance in relation to your goals and responsibilities.
onboarding.methods.eisenhower.feature2: Sort work into four combinations of those two dimensions.
onboarding.methods.eisenhower.feature3: Make room for important work before it becomes urgent.
onboarding.methods.para.name: PARA
onboarding.methods.para.description: Organize information around what it supports now, using four broad categories.
onboarding.methods.para.example: Notes for a current home-improvement project stay together. When the project ends, its supporting material can move to the archive.
onboarding.methods.para.effort: Decide where material belongs and revisit that decision as its purpose changes.
onboarding.methods.para.limits: PARA is an information structure, not a complete system for next actions, reminders, prioritization or developing ideas.
onboarding.methods.para.feature0: Projects: active efforts with a defined outcome.
onboarding.methods.para.feature1: Areas: ongoing responsibilities that need attention.
onboarding.methods.para.feature2: Resources: topics and material that may be useful.
onboarding.methods.para.feature3: Archives: material from the other categories that is no longer active.
onboarding.methods.zettelkasten.name: Zettelkasten
onboarding.methods.zettelkasten.descript: Develop your thinking through a growing collection of notes that refer to and build on one another.
onboarding.methods.zettelkasten.example: A reading note connects to an earlier argument and a contrasting example, giving you a starting point for a new piece of writing.
onboarding.methods.zettelkasten.effort: Write, connect and revisit notes. Useful relationships take consideration; a graph of links alone is not the method.
onboarding.methods.zettelkasten.limits: Zettelkasten does not manage deadlines or replace general document filing. A project ending does not necessarily make its connected ideas obsolete.
onboarding.methods.zettelkasten.feature0: Give notes stable addresses so you can refer to them.
onboarding.methods.zettelkasten.feature1: Follow lines of thought and branch into related ideas.
onboarding.methods.zettelkasten.feature3: Use keyword entry points and references to sources.
